podcast.title: Roadie for Nirvana, then Joined Soundgarden
podcast.body: Ben Shepherd worked as a roadie for Nirvana before securing his position as a member of the band Soundgarden, a prominent figure in the Seattle music scene. "And later Ben Shepard roadied for Nirvana before he got his gig with Soundgarden."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Successor to Yamamoto
podcast.body: Ben Shepherd eventually took over as Soundgarden's bassist, stepping into the role after Hiro Yamamoto's departure in the late 1980s. "Ben Shepard would eventually take over as the band's bassist."

xref.title: Ben Shepherd's Bass Playing Style
xref.body: Bassist Ben Shepherd was noted for his distinctive playing, often using power chords on his bass, which contributed to Soundgarden's heavy sound. "Ben Shepherd of SoundGarden practically played power chords on his bass sometime."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ben Shepherd's Enduring Role – Roadie to Bassist
xref.body: Ben Shepherd eventually replaced Jason Everman as Soundgarden's bassist and has held the position since. Before joining Soundgarden, Shepherd was active in the Seattle scene, playing in bands like March of Crimes (briefly with Stone Gossard) and Tick Dolly Roe (with Chad Channing), and even freelanced as Nirvana's roadie before being briefly considered for their second guitarist role. "But that was still okay because he auditioned for Soundgarden again and got the job, and he still has that job today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ben Shepherd's Near Miss – Ejected for Kurt Cobain's Vision
xref.body: Ben Shepherd, later the bassist for Soundgarden, was asked to join Nirvana as a second guitarist in the period leading up to the release of *Nevermind*. However, like Jason Everman before him, he was ejected from the band because Kurt Cobain wanted to maintain Nirvana as a three-piece. "Ben was asked to be the second guitarist in Nirvana, doing essentially what Jason Everman had been asked to do the year before. But like Jason, he was ejected from the band when Kurt wanted to keep it a three piece."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chad Channing's Drumming Tenure – Introduction by a Friend
xref.body: Chad Channing became Nirvana's drummer for a period after a friend introduced him to Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic. Prior to this, Channing had been playing in a band called Tick Dolly Roe with Ben Shepherd, whose departure to Nirvana led to the end of Tick Dolly Roe. "One of Chad's friends introduced him to Kurt Cobain and Chris Nova Selaich, and he became Nirvana's drummer for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Seattle Band – Brief Stone Gossard Connection
xref.body: March of Crimes was a band in Seattle that featured Ben Shepherd, who would later become Soundgarden's bassist. Notably, a teenage Stone Gossard, future member of Mother Love Bone and Pearl Jam, briefly played guitar in this group. "Ben had been around Seattle for years, once playing in a band called March of Crimes, which briefly featured a teenage guitarist named Stone Gossard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ended by Drummer's Departure to Nirvana – Impact of Chad Channing
xref.body: Tick Dolly Roe was a band that included Ben Shepherd and Chad Channing. The group dissolved after Channing was introduced to Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic by a friend and subsequently became Nirvana's drummer for a while. "So that was it for Tick Tock Dolly, but Ben Shepard didn't mind, because he freelanced as Nirvana's Rody for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
